Question: Which node in the generative model represents the latent variable?
Evidence:
[E1] (text, Section Figure 1, page 4): Figure 1: Figure 1a presents the generative story of our model. Figure 1b illustrates the inference net- work using the reparametrization trick to perform variational inference on our model. Shaded nodes are observed; double circles indicate deterministic transformations of parent nodes. w y η θ r α c B Ni D (a) Generative model r µ σ π c y w ϵ linear linear D (b) Inference model
[E2] (text, Section 1, page 1): and Blei , 2008 ), which jointly models words and labels (e.g., ratings) as being generated from a latent representation, and sparse additive generative models (SAGE; Eisenstein et al. , 2011 ), which assumes that observed covariates (e.g., author ideology) have a sparse effect on the relative probabilities of words given topics. The structural topic model (STM; Roberts et al. , 2014 ), which adds correlations between topics to SAGE, is also widely used, but like SAGE it is limited in the types of metadata it can efﬁciently make use of, and how that metadata is used. Note that in this work we will distinguish labels (metadata that are generated jointly with words from latent topic representations) from covariates (observed metadata that inﬂuence the distribution of labels and words). The ability to create variations of LDA such as those listed above has been limited by the expertise needed to develop custom inference algorithms for each model. As a result, it is rare to see such variations being widely used in practice. In this work, we take advantage of recent advances in variational methods ( Kingma and Welling , 2014 ; Rezende et al. , 2014 ; Miao et al. , 2016 ; Srivastava and Sutton , 2017 ) to facilitate approximate Bayesian inference without requiring model-speciﬁc derivations , and propose a general neural framework for topic models with metadata, SCHOLAR . 1
[E3] (text, Section 1, page 2): In presenting this particular model, we emphasize not only its ability to adapt to the characteristics of the data, but the extent to which the VAE approach to inference provides a powerful framework for latent variable modeling that suggests the possibility of many further extensions. Our implementation is available at https://github. com/dallascard/scholar .

These claims failed the checks; write corrected claims to replace them:
- "The latent variable is represented by the double circle in the generative model.": support check: The claim states that the latent variable is represented by the double circle in the generative model. However, the evidence provided refers to the inference network in Figure 1b, not the generative model in Figure 1a. The evidence indicates that double circles indicate deterministic transformations of parent nodes, not latent variables.
- "The generative model in Figure 1a includes nodes labeled w, y, η, θ, r, α, c, B, Ni, D, and D.": support check: The claim lists the nodes w, y, η, θ, r, α, c, B, Ni, D, and D in the generative model. However, the evidence provided in Figure 1a lists the nodes w, y, η, θ, r, α, c, B, Ni, D, and D, but it does not specify which of these nodes are latent variables. The evidence does not provide enough information to confirm that all these nodes are latent variables.
